To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structure of a family GH‐19 chitinase in a complex with a tetrasaccharide was successfully solved, which revealed the substrate‐binding mode, and that the crystallographic results were further confirmed by NMR binding experiments.

the crystal structure of the 26‐kD rye chitinase in complex with an N-acetylglucosaminotetramer revealed the oligosacchardie-binding mode of a family 19 chitinase and that this mode is consistent with that from NMR binding studies in solution.
the crystal structure of a family GH‐19 chitinase in a complex with a chitin oligosacharide revealed the binding mode and the crystallographic evidence was further confirmed by NMR spectroscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystallographic and NMR characterization of a 26 kDa GH19 chitnase from rye seeds, which is the first crystallographically characterized member of family 19 chitinases.
the structural and functional analysis of a 26 kDa GH19 family chitinase from the seeds of rye (Secale cerele).
the crystal structure and the chitin oligosacrharide‐binding mode, which is the first crystallographical data showing the oligochitin oligosacchride‐binding mode of GH19 chitinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RSC‐c binds to (GlcNA)4 through the aglycon binding site, subsite +1 to subsite +4, and that the Trp residue located at subsite +4 is essential for substrate binding.

the aglycon of the substrate is bound in an ‘open’ manner in the aglycon binding site, subsites −1, +1, +3, +4, and +5, and the chitooligosaccharide moiety is bound in a ‘closed’ manner in subsites +2 and +3.
the crystal structure and the solution NMR experiments are consistent with the binding of the (GlcNAch4)4 oligosaccharides at subsites +1 to +4 of the RSC‐c enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the crystal structure and the NMR data are complementary to each other in the sense that crystallographic data are useful for the identification of the binding site and the binding mode of oligosaccharides, and NMR data are useful for identifying amino acids that interact with substrates.
RSC‐c has a ‘loopful’, or a large loop, at the aglycon binding site, which is different from the other GH19 chitinases whose aglycon‐ and glycan‐binding sites have been reported.

the crystallographic and NMR data are consistent with each other, and that the crystallographically determined substrate‐binding mode is also consistent with the enzymatic data obtained from the mutational experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallographic and NMR data obtained from the complex of RSC‐ c and (GlcNAch)4 are consistent with each other.
the aglycon site of the GH19 chitinases can be used to accommodate a tetramer of the chitin substrate.
the aglycon of a family GH20 chitinase can be bound to the aglycon binding site, which is located on the opposite side of the catalytic cleft.
